draft.title: Narrative voice
card: Voice is the personality of the narrator that a reader hears in the writing. Two narrators can tell the same event and still sound completely different.
Word choice
The words a narrator picks give them a character. Slang and jokes sound chatty and young. Formal, careful words sound stiff or serious.
Sentence rhythm
The length and pace of sentences set how the narrator sounds. Short, quick sentences can sound nervous or blunt. Long, winding ones can sound dreamy or talkative.
Attitude
What the narrator seems to feel about people and events also shapes voice. A narrator might sound proud, shy, bored or full of wonder.
draft.remember: Voice is who seems to be talking, built from word choice, sentence rhythm and attitude.

a.q: Which best describes what a narrative voice is?
opts: The personality of the narrator heard in the writing
The order in which the events of a story are told
The sound of a character's words when read aloud
The point in the story where the conflict is solved
a.why: Voice is the personality a reader hears in the narrator's words. Reading aloud can help you hear it, but voice is not about sound itself: it comes from word choice, rhythm and attitude on the page.
a.clue: Think about who seems to be talking to you.

b.q: A narrator complains about a itchy jumper using words such as ugh and seriously, and calls it the worst day ever. Which feature most helps create a chatty, grumpy voice?
opts: Casual words such as ugh and seriously
Long, flowing sentences full of detail
Formal words that sound careful and polite
A calm attitude that shows no strong feelings
b.why: Casual words like ugh and seriously, with the complaining attitude, make the narrator sound chatty and grumpy. Formal words would sound careful, and a calm attitude would not suit someone calling the day the worst ever.
b.clue: Look at the kind of words the narrator picks.

a.best: The personality of the narrator heard in the writing

b.best: Casual words such as ugh and seriously
